answer: Unique silicon fingerprint enrollment binds each agent identity to one PUF die’s challenge-response and manufacturer certificate, rejecting any response reused across identities despite glacier-slow extraction attempts. At enrollment the PUF signs a nonce from a local beacon, so recorded responses cannot be replayed or shared. Each identity then requires its own ferrous tamper-mesh chip powered and physically challenged, costing an attacker one distinct device plus acquisition and handling per identity.
